title: Scientific verification: He initialization keeps deep ReLU activations stable

problem.description: The knowledge record EXP-000006 claims that naive weight initialization (std=1.0) causes activation variance to explode exponentially with depth in ReLU networks (NaN or dead loss), while He initialization (std=sqrt(2/fan_in)) keeps variance stable across layers. This claim was verified once with a single check; this run re-verifies it scientifically with controlled experiments, negative controls, boundary conditions and regression tests.
problem.symptoms: deep ReLU networks show NaN loss within the first updates, or a dead-flat loss regardless of learning rate; activation histograms grow/shrink by orders of magnitude with depth
problem.expectedBehavior: forward pass through an untrained deep ReLU network preserves activation scale within roughly an order of magnitude at EVERY depth when weights use He init std=sqrt(2/fan_in); naive std=1.0 explodes by ~fan_in/2 per layer
problem.actualBehavior: to be measured: run controlled simulations with both init schemes at multiple depths and measure mean squared activation
problem.facts: Var(y) ~ n * E[w^2] * Var(x) for y=Wx with n inputs; ReLU zeroes half the units; He init sets E[w^2]=2/n
problem.assumptions: python3 with math/random is available on the workspace (probed earlier: python3 present); float64 semantics
problem.environment: user's local machine via the bridge extension, Linux, python3
problem.constraints: no external dependencies — stdlib only; each test must complete within its timeout

hypothesis.text: In a 20-layer, 64-unit ReLU network, naive std=1.0 initialization multiplies the mean squared activation by ~fan_in/2 per layer (exploding to >1e6), while He initialization std=sqrt(2/64)=0.177 keeps mean squared activation within [0.01, 100] at every depth. A smaller 5-layer network with He init should ALSO stay stable (boundary condition), and a negative control with deliberately undersized init (std=0.01) should VANISH (<1e-6) — confirming that the stability specifically depends on the 2/fan_in scaling, not on any init.

hypothesis.supportingEvidence: the original single-check verification of EXP-000006 (20-layer naive=1e28 vs He~1) stored in the knowledge evidence
hypothesis.contradictingEvidence: none observed yet — this run is designed to look for it
